vikisozluk_etimolojiler.metin: From Classical Syriac ܫܒܛ (šḇāṭ), ultimately from Akkadian 𒌚𒀾 (Šabāṭum). Cognate with Hebrew שְׁבָט (sh'vat, “Shebat, the eleventh month of the Hebrew lunisolar calendar”).
Borrowing from Aramaic שִׁבּוּטָא (šebbūṭā), ܫܰܒܽܘܛܳܐ (šabbūṭā), from שְׁבַט (šḇaṭ), ܫܰܒܶܛ (šabeṭ, “to beat out; to straighten”).
Singulative noun composed of شَبُّوط (šabbūṭ, “carp”) + ـَة (-a).
See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.
